forecast = a report that says what the weather will be
cloudy = with a lot of cloud and little sun
foggy = with thick cloud near the ground that is hard to see through
lightning = a flash of light in the sky during a storm
thunder = the loud noise that follows lightning
hail = frozen rain that falls as small balls of ice
drought = a long time with little or no rain
flood = water covering land that is usually dry
hurricane = a very strong tropical storm with fast winds
climate = the usual weather in a place over many years
environment = the air, water, land and living things around us
pollution = dirty air, water or land caused by people
recycle = to turn used materials into new products
rubbish = things you throw away
litter = rubbish left on the ground in a public place
endangered = at risk of disappearing as a species
extinct = no longer existing as a species
wildlife = animals and plants living in nature, not kept by people
habitat = the natural place where an animal or plant lives
rainforest = a thick, wet forest in a hot part of the world
desert = a very dry area with little rain
island = a piece of land with water all around it
valley = low land between hills or mountains
waterfall = a place where a river falls from a high point
volcano = a mountain that can send out hot rock and ash
earthquake = a sudden, strong shaking of the ground
protect = to keep someone or something safe from harm
global warming = the slow rise in the Earth's temperature
greenhouse effect = gases in the air that trap heat from the sun
renewable energy = power from the sun, wind or water that will not run out
species = a group of animals or plants of the same kind
wild animal = an animal that does not live with people as a pet
insect = a small animal with six legs, such as a bee or ant
plant = a living thing that grows in soil, such as a tree or flower
harvest = the time when crops are collected; to collect them
season = one of the four parts of the year with typical weather
sunny = with a lot of sun and few clouds
rainy = with a lot of rain
windy = with a strong wind
snowy = with snow falling or on the ground
storm = very bad weather with strong wind, rain or snow
blizzard = a severe snowstorm with strong wind
heatwave = several very hot days in a row
frost = ice that forms on surfaces when it is very cold
freezing = below 0°C; extremely cold
mild = not very hot and not very cold
boiling = informal: extremely hot weather
breeze = a light, pleasant wind
gale = a very strong wind
rainbow = an arc of colours in the sky after rain
sunshine = light and heat from the sun
shade = a cooler place where the sun does not shine
puddle = a small pool of water on the ground after rain
mud = wet, soft earth
soil = the top layer of earth in which plants grow
rock = hard natural stone in the ground or mountains
pebble = a small, smooth stone, often on a beach
sand = very small grains of rock, as on a beach
forest = a large area of trees
woods = a smaller area of trees, often near a town
meadow = a field of grass and wild flowers
field = an area of land used for crops or grass
mountain = a very high area of land
hill = a raised area of land, smaller than a mountain
river = a large natural stream of water that flows to the sea
lake = a large area of water surrounded by land
pond = a small area of still water
ocean = a very large sea
wave = a moving ridge of water on the sea
tide = the regular rise and fall of the sea
cliff = a high, steep rock face, often by the sea
cave = a large hole in rock or underground
tree = a tall plant with a wooden trunk
leaf = the flat green part of a plant
branch = an arm of a tree that grows from the trunk
root = the part of a plant that grows under the ground
seed = the small part of a plant from which a new plant can grow
flower = the colourful part of a plant that makes seeds
grass = the short green plants that cover lawns and fields
bush = a plant with many woody stems, smaller than a tree
oak = a large tree that produces acorns
pine = an evergreen tree with needles and cones
bird = an animal with feathers and wings that usually flies
nest = a home that a bird builds for its eggs
feather = one of the light parts that cover a bird's body
beak = the hard mouth of a bird
wing = the part a bird or insect uses to fly
fish = an animal that lives in water and has gills
whale = a very large sea animal that breathes air
dolphin = an intelligent sea animal that looks like a small whale
shark = a large fish with sharp teeth
bear = a large wild animal with thick fur
wolf = a wild animal like a large dog that lives in packs
fox = a wild animal with a thick tail and red-brown fur
deer = a wild animal with long legs; males often have antlers
rabbit = a small animal with long ears that lives in holes
squirrel = a small animal with a bushy tail that lives in trees
hedgehog = a small animal with spikes on its back
bee = a flying insect that makes honey and can sting
butterfly = an insect with large colourful wings
spider = a small animal with eight legs that makes webs
ant = a small insect that lives in large groups
worm = a long, thin animal that lives in soil
paw = the foot of an animal such as a dog or cat
fur = the thick hair that covers some animals
tail = the long part at the back of an animal
hibernate = to sleep through the winter
migrate = to travel to another place for part of the year
nature reserve = an area of land protected for plants and animals
national park = a large protected area of beautiful landscape
zoo = a place where wild animals are kept for people to see
safari = a trip to see wild animals in their natural habitat
compost = rotted plants used to make soil richer
landfill = a place where rubbish is buried in the ground
plastic = a light material used for bottles and bags; it lasts a long time
packaging = the paper, plastic or boxes around products
save energy = to use less electricity or gas
carbon footprint = the amount of greenhouse gas your life produces
deforestation = cutting down forests on a large scale
oil spill = when oil from a ship or well pollutes the sea
poacher = a person who hunts animals illegally
breed = to keep animals so they have young; also a type of animal
hunt = to chase and kill wild animals
organic farming = growing food without most chemical sprays
pesticide = a chemical that kills insects on crops
climate change = long-term change in the Earth's weather, often caused by people
